description.text: Justice for Exonerees Act This bill increases the maximum amount of damages that an individual who was unjustly convicted and incarcerated may be awarded and requires that this amount be adjusted annually for inflation.

latestAction.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

aiDescription.summary: The Justice for Exonerees Act raises the cap in 28 U.S.C. 2513(e) from $50,000 to $70,000 and requires annual CPI-based inflation adjustments to awards under that subsection. It covers persons unjustly convicted and imprisoned who obtain damages under that federal statute against the United States.

impact.summary: The bill raises the maximum federal damage award for an unjust conviction and imprisonment under 28 U.S.C. §2513 from $50,000 to $70,000 and requires annual inflation adjustments tied to the Consumer Price Index. It affects exonerees, the Department of Justice, federal courts, and Treasury.
